article.title: Why AI Agents Need Idempotent Actions
article.why: 理解 Agent tool-use 的交易安全：permission 之外，還需要 retry-safe 與 idempotency。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
An AI agent that can take actions through software tools faces a practical engineering problem that ordinary chat systems do not: the same action may accidentally be executed more than once. A network timeout, retry, duplicate message, or uncertain response can cause the agent to repeat a request. If the action is harmless, this may only waste time. If the action sends money, creates a ticket, places an order, or emails a customer, duplication can be expensive.

This is why idempotency matters. An idempotent operation can be repeated without creating additional unintended effects. For example, ‘set the account status to active’ can be designed to have the same final result whether it is called once or several times. ‘Add $100 to the balance,’ however, is not naturally idempotent because every repeated call changes the result again.

Many APIs handle this with an idempotency key. Before an agent performs a high-impact action, the system creates a unique identifier for that intended transaction. If the same request is retried with the same key, the receiving service recognizes that it has already processed the action and returns the original result instead of executing it again.

This design is especially useful for agents because agents may plan, call tools, inspect responses, and retry autonomously. A human operator can sometimes notice that a payment probably succeeded despite a timeout. An agent may simply see ‘no response’ and try again. Without protection, reasonable retry behavior can become duplicate execution.

Idempotency is not the same as permission control. Permissions answer whether the agent is allowed to perform an action. Idempotency answers what happens if an allowed action is repeated. A secure system needs both. Human approval also does not solve duplication by itself: one approved action can still be submitted twice if the technical workflow retries incorrectly.

Teams should identify which tools create external side effects. Read-only searches are usually less dangerous, while writes, purchases, notifications, deletions, and state transitions deserve stronger treatment. Tool definitions can expose whether an operation supports an idempotency key, whether retries are safe, and what result should be checked before trying again.

Logging is also important. The system should record the intended action, idempotency key, tool call, response, and retry history. If an incident occurs, operators need to distinguish between two genuine user requests and one request that was accidentally executed twice.

The principle is simple: autonomous systems should be designed for uncertain networks and imperfect execution. Better reasoning does not eliminate timeouts or duplicate messages. When an agent can change the outside world, reliability depends not only on choosing the right action but also on making sure one intended action becomes one real-world effect.

Another useful pattern is check-before-write. Before creating a resource, the agent can query whether an equivalent resource already exists. This is not a complete substitute for idempotency because two requests can still race with each other, but it adds defense in depth. For destructive operations, a workflow may also separate ‘prepare’ from ‘commit,’ so the agent first generates an exact action plan and then sends a final transactional request.

Failure handling should be explicit in the tool contract. The agent needs to know which errors are safe to retry, which require waiting, and which should stop the workflow and escalate to a human. A timeout is different from a confirmed rejection. Treating every error as ‘try again’ is dangerous.

The business impact is broader than engineering quality. Duplicate invoices, repeated customer messages, or double-created support cases reduce trust and create cleanup work. As organizations give agents more autonomy, transaction safety becomes part of AI governance. The question is no longer only, ‘Did the model intend the right action?’ It is also, ‘Did the surrounding system guarantee that the intended action was executed exactly as safely as the business requires?’
paragraphs.zh:
能透過軟體工具採取行動的 AI Agent，會遇到一般聊天系統沒有的工程問題：同一個動作可能被意外執行多次。網路 timeout、retry、重複訊息或不確定回應，都可能讓 Agent 重送請求。若只是無害操作，最多浪費時間；如果是付款、建立工單、下單或寄客戶信件，重複執行就可能造成實際損失。

這就是 idempotency 重要的原因。Idempotent operation 可以被重複呼叫，而不會產生額外的非預期效果。例如『把帳戶狀態設成 active』可以設計成呼叫一次或多次都得到相同最終狀態；但『帳戶餘額加 100 美元』天生不是 idempotent，因為每重複一次結果都會再變。

很多 API 用 idempotency key 處理這個問題。Agent 執行高影響動作前，系統為該次交易建立唯一識別碼。如果同一請求以相同 key 重試，接收端會知道它已處理過，直接回傳原本結果，而不是再執行一次。

這對 Agent 特別重要，因為 Agent 會自行規劃、呼叫工具、檢查回應與 retry。人類有時會從情境判斷『付款可能其實成功，只是 timeout』；Agent 可能只看到沒有回應就重試。沒有保護時，合理的 retry 會變成 duplicate execution。

Idempotency 和 permission control 不同。Permission 回答 Agent 是否有權做某個動作；idempotency 回答這個合法動作被重複送出時會發生什麼。安全系統兩者都需要。Human approval 也無法單獨解決重複問題，因為一次已批准的動作仍可能因技術重試而被送兩次。

團隊應先辨識哪些 tools 會產生 external side effects。Read-only 搜尋通常較安全，而 write、purchase、notification、delete、state transition 應有更強保護。Tool definition 可以標示是否支援 idempotency key、retry 是否安全，以及重試前應檢查什麼結果。

Logging 也很重要。系統應記錄 intended action、idempotency key、tool call、response 與 retry history。事故發生時，才能區分兩個真正的使用者請求，與同一請求被誤執行兩次。

核心原則是：自主系統必須假設網路不確定、執行也可能不完美。更好的 reasoning 不會消除 timeout 或 duplicate message。當 Agent 能改變外部世界，可靠性不只取決於是否選對 action，也取決於能否保證一個 intended action 只產生一個真實效果。

另一個做法是 check-before-write。建立資源前，Agent 先查是否已有等價資源。這不能完全取代 idempotency，因為兩個請求仍可能 race，但可增加 defense in depth。高風險操作也可把 prepare 與 commit 分開，先產生精確動作計畫，再送最後 transaction。

Failure handling 應寫進 tool contract。Agent 必須知道哪些 error 可安全 retry、哪些要等待、哪些應停止並 escalate 給人。Timeout 和明確拒絕不是同一種錯誤，把所有 error 都當成『再試一次』很危險。

這不只是工程品質問題。重複 invoice、重複客戶訊息或雙重建立工單都會降低信任並增加清理成本。當組織提高 Agent 自主性，transaction safety 也會成為 AI governance 的一部分。
paragraphs.ja:
Software toolを使って行動するAI Agentには、通常のchat systemにはない問題があります。同じactionが誤って複数回実行される可能性です。network timeout、retry、duplicate message、不確かなresponseによってAgentがrequestを繰り返すことがあります。送金、ticket作成、注文、顧客メールなら重複は高コストです。

そのためidempotencyが重要です。Idempotent operationは繰り返しても追加の意図しない影響を生みません。『account statusをactiveにする』は何回呼んでも同じ最終状態にできますが、『balanceへ100ドル追加する』は呼ぶたびに結果が変わります。

多くのAPIはidempotency keyを使います。高impact actionの前に一意のtransaction identifierを作り、同じkeyでretryされた場合、serviceは既に処理済みと認識して元のresultを返します。

Agentはplan、tool call、response確認、retryを自律的に行うため、この設計が特に重要です。人間ならtimeout後に『支払いは成功したかもしれない』と判断できますが、Agentはno responseを見て単純に再試行する可能性があります。

Idempotencyはpermission controlとは別です。Permissionは行動してよいか、idempotencyは許可済みactionが重複したらどうなるかを扱います。Human approvalだけでも重複送信は防げません。

外部side effectを持つtoolを特定し、write、purchase、notification、deletion、state transitionなどを強く保護します。Tool definitionにはidempotency keyの対応、retry safety、再試行前の確認方法を含められます。

Loggingではintended action、idempotency key、tool call、response、retry historyを残します。incident時に二つの正規requestと一つの重複実行を区別できる必要があります。

Autonomous systemは不確かなnetworkと不完全なexecutionを前提に設計すべきです。better reasoningでもtimeoutやduplicate messageは消えません。一つのintended actionを一つのreal-world effectにする仕組みが必要です。

check-before-writeも有効です。resource作成前に同等resourceが存在するか確認します。競合状態を完全には防げませんがdefense in depthになります。高risk操作ではprepareとcommitを分離する方法もあります。

Failure handlingはtool contractで明示します。どのerrorがsafe to retryか、待つべきか、停止してhumanへescalateすべきかを区別します。timeoutとconfirmed rejectionは違います。

重複invoice、customer message、support caseは信頼を落としcleanup costを生みます。Agent autonomyが高まるほどtransaction safetyはAI governanceの一部になります。

Give each transaction a unique key.

Idempotency and validation provide defense in depth.
The tool contract should state whether an error is safe to retry.

grammar.body: 強調可靠性不只取決於選對 action，也取決於執行安全。

business.example: Before enabling automation, is this operation retry-safe?
What prevents duplicate execution after a timeout?

quiz.question: What problem does an idempotency key solve?
quiz.answer: It prevents the same intended transaction from being executed multiple times during retries.
